$comment: Binds every one of DGA’s 58 checklist criteria to the checks that can evidence it, or marks it manual with the reason no measurement settles it. The manual entries are the honest part: 49 of 58 rows cannot be answered from a rendered page today, and each carries DGA’s own reference URL so a human can go and judge it.
$statusSource: Data validation on column E of the supplied workbook. These four strings are DGA’s, verbatim, and must not be paraphrased.
$noButtonCriterion: The checklist has no Button row. Buttons appear only inside #36 (interaction design), so the heaviest component finding this tool produces — buttons off radius-sm — belongs to no criterion of its own.
$accessibility: A1, A2 and A3 map to NO criterion: the checklist contains no contrast, focus, keyboard or ARIA item, and inventing one would put words in DGA's mouth. A4 is the single exception and it is not an exception to the rule — criterion #28 explicitly names touch interactions on small screens, and target size is direct evidence for that. A4 is therefore used as evidence for a MOBILE USABILITY criterion, not smuggled in as an accessibility criterion. All four are additionally reported in their own section, which is informational and never counted in the checklist totals. DGA's AssessmentCriteria page does name إمكانية الوصول as assessment category one, so DGA's two artefacts disagree; that is recorded, not resolved.
